summary:
The bill makes fiscal year 2025 appropriations for energy and water development and related agencies, generally from Treasury funds not otherwise appropriated, with numerous no-year and two-year availabilities, transfers, offsetting collections, reprogramming controls, and funding prohibitions. Title I appropriates Corps of Engineers–Civil funds, including Investigations ($159 million), Construction ($3.01 billion), Mississippi River and Tributaries ($370 million), Operation and Maintenance ($5.714 billion), Regulatory Program ($218 million), FUSRAP ($200 million), Flood Control and Coastal Emergencies ($45 million), Expenses ($231 million), the Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works ($5 million), and WIFIA administrative expenses ($5 million). It requires adherence to work plans, establishes Corps reprogramming thresholds and reporting (§101), authorizes a transfer to the Fish and Wildlife Service for fisheries mitigation (§104), restricts Lake Erie open-lake dredged-material placement (§105), bars specified Wolf Creek Dam water-supply study funding (§106), requires WOTUS guidance production (§108), freezes specified 33 U.S.C. 701n eligibility absent express authorization (§109), and prospectively bars Army regulations prohibiting lawful firearm possession at covered water resources development projects (§110).

Title II funds the Central Utah Project and Bureau of Reclamation, including Water and Related Resources ($1.773 billion), the Central Valley Project Restoration Fund from collections, California Bay-Delta Restoration ($33 million), and Policy and Administration ($66.794 million), with transfer authorities and Reclamation reprogramming limitations (§201). It extends and amends authorities under the Calfed Bay-Delta Authorization Act (§203), the Reclamation States Emergency Drought Relief Act of 1991 (§204), the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, 43 U.S.C. 3202(a)(2) (§207), and WIIN Act §§4004, 4007, 4009, and 4013 (§§208–209), and increases authorizations in 43 U.S.C. 390h and the Water Desalination Act of 1996 (§209). Sections 205–206 impose conditions and operational directives concerning Central Valley Project/State Water Project consultations and operations.

Title III appropriates Department of Energy, NNSA, defense cleanup, power marketing, and FERC accounts, including major funding for EERE, Nuclear Energy, Science, Weapons Activities, Defense Nuclear Nonproliferation, Naval Reactors, and Defense Environmental Cleanup. DOE general provisions impose award-notification, multiyear, reprogramming, nuclear-safety, project-cost, petroleum-reserve, China/Russia-access, procurement, Justice40, NEPA categorical-exclusion, and other restrictions (§§301–314). Section 315 amends Natural Gas Act §3, 15 U.S.C. 717b, to assign FERC exclusive authority over natural-gas import/export facility applications, deem imports and exports in the public interest, and preserve presidential sanctions and emergency authorities. Section 317 transfers specified unobligated balances to DOE Nuclear Energy for small modular and advanced reactor awards and amends Public Law 117-169 funding levels.

Title IV funds specified independent agencies and commissions, including ARC, DNFSB, regional commissions, NRC, and NWTRB, with NRC fee-offset and reprogramming provisions (§§401–402). Title V contains government-wide riders on lobbying, transfers, pornography blocking, spent nuclear fuel consolidated interim storage, CRT, equity executive orders, religious/moral marriage-belief discrimination, COVID-19 mandates, Wuhan Institute funding, flags, major rules, ecosystem valuation guidance, Columbia Basin reimbursement limits, and specified DOE energy-conservation rules; §515 establishes a $0 spending reduction account. The Act is cited as the “Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2025.”
